questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I could have my courses pre-approved here and then i wanted to go somewhere where i could go without flying for ethical reason. It also seemed feasible for me to learn swedish quite well even though i would only be there for a semester which was a plus.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The high score is primarily based on good social and cultural experiences i have had in sweden but not based on how the experience was academically

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. Everything is on their website and they are pretty responsive by email

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not really any. They have quite a good public transport system. Just make sure not to pay for the "Arlanda express" train when you arrive as it is unecessary and very expensive.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Quite difficult. I found my accommodation through Stockholms Bostandsförmedling where i was lucky to find acommodation that did not require me to have a swedish ID. My tip sould be to get in as many house queues as possible early on (especially SSSB and bostadtsförmedlingen) and maybe get a temporary swedish ID early on as well ("coordination number") where you have to go physically to sweden for them to verify your identity. I also was able to get a couple of offers on Casa Blocket and various facebook groups.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Its fine. A lot of nature is close to they city which is a plus when you live far off campus. The train system is quite well connected so dont panic if you dont get accommodation on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I said that i was basically willing to take any accommodation they could find me but i was still rejected.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: not that bad

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I honestly cant remember but it was easy

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: i dont remember. Probably a instructive email

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: i did not have any troubles. Just be aware that they use a block structure with A, B, C and D representing their own 7.5 ECTS block and that you can the study a course e.g. on 100% time or 50% etc.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not find the psychology courses very good but i also had to select courses that were not taught for the actual clinical psychology programme but freestanding courses instead. They were not all bad though. I liked the psychology of perception course a lot

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: As i said, the level was quite low i thougt

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More exclusively lectures and then sometimes small group projects that my fellow students did not seem to motivated to do unfortunately.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Psychology of perception
Clinical psychology
Cognitive psychology
Stress and Health

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Psychology of perception and cognitive psychology were good i thougt

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are student unions, pubs and Erasmus activities that are all good fun and a nice way of meeting people

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Student union point hunt, student pubs (and sittninger at the student pubs) as well as hikes and longer trips with Erasmus student network (i had a good trip to Gotland)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Gotland, Nacka reservaten, second hand stores west from Slussen station and the lunch deal at Falafelkungen by Odenplan

My coolets experience was probably exploring Klövbergsgrottorna but you have to be a bit prepared to do that if you are not with anyone that knows the caves

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy but as always it is difficult to make local friends as they already have busy lives so i found a lot of relief in hanging out with other interantional students who were more open. Eventually, some swedes will hopefully also open up a little:)

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the events at the university and be a little brave. There is also a whatsapp group with only erasmus students that you could make an event in. I invited some poeple to the photographic museum and got a lot of friends early on=)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language is challenging to speak but i just kept at it

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the fika culture and the willingness to explore the nature

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Dont procrastinate looking for an apartment
2. Dont flock up with only danes - the most rewarding part of this trip for me was meeting people from all over the world
3. Try to speak swedish and sign up for the swedish language course - It is not that difficult once you start doing it frequently

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Maybe that they use BankID for a lot of things like Swish which is their money transaction app. You might wanna consider getting that early on but you need a temporary swedish ID for that.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends i made along the way;)

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Moving into an unfurnished aparment and having to aquire everything

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
